The CDI runtime contract for GPU images, and the ONLY layer that owns it.

A GPU container does not get its driver from the image: the kernel module is
host-global, so the driver user-space must come from the host, injected per container
(`--device nvidia.com/gpu=all`, via the NVIDIA container toolkit's CDI spec and its
runtime hook). An image that bakes its own driver user-space does not merely duplicate
that — it WINS the SONAME resolution, because the injection mounts the host's VERSIONED
files (libnvidia-ml.so.615.78.08, ...) and the image's own newer copy
(libnvidia-ml.so.620.70.06) stays visible next to them, so `libnvidia-ml.so.1` resolves
to the baked one. `nvidia-smi` then exits 18 with "Driver/library version mismatch", and
every consumer that estimates free memory through NVML — ollama among them — silently
degrades to CPU while answering normally. Measured on CachyOS, October 2026:
host module 615.78.08 against a baked userspace 620.70.06, ollama offloading 0/29
layers. opencharly/layer-cuda#21.

So this layer does exactly three things, and every GPU image composes it:

  1. REMOVES the host-coupled driver user-space and the `nvidia*` binaries that a
     distro package manager installs as a side effect of installing the CUDA toolkit
     (`pacman -S cuda` depends on `nvidia-utils`; `dnf install cuda-nvcc` pulls
     `nvidia-driver` userspace on some distros).
  2. PROVES, at build time and again at check time, that none of them remain — including
     the versioned files, because the CDI create-symlinks hook re-creates each SONAME
     link from whatever versioned file it finds.
  3. PROVES, at check time, that the container actually resolved the INJECTED driver and
     that its version equals the running kernel module's.

What this layer deliberately does NOT remove: the Vulkan/OpenCL ICD JSONs. They name a
SONAME (`libGLX_nvidia.so.0`), not a version, so the link the injection creates
satisfies them — which is why they are part of the contract rather than a violation of
it.

## Acceptance plan

This candy's `plan:` — the runnable spec `charly check` executes against a live deployment. `check:` steps are idempotent probes; `run:` steps change state.

| Intent | Step |
|---|---|
| `run` | no host-coupled driver library is baked — the injection is the only provider |
| `run` | no host-coupled nvidia binary is baked — the injection is the only provider |
| `check` | the container resolved the INJECTED host driver, and its version equals the running kernel module's |
